answer: Unique-work challenge issuance. Each agent must answer a fresh, randomly seeded problem whose solution is checked for novelty against a shared ledger, so a copied reply is rejected before it earns standing—like a vine that only fruits on new growth. The system records every submitted solution in a public orchard of prior outputs, and any duplicate fails the uniqueness test outright. Attackers must therefore produce genuinely new work per identity, paying real compute and time for each, with no nectar of reuse to spread across clones.
